3. The defendant No.1 contested the suit by filing a written statement denying the plaintiffs case contending, inter-alia, that the land of CS khatian No. 145 belonged to Darikanath and Rajkumar in equal shares. The entire land of that khatian was put to auction in Title Execution Case No.133 of 1944 and that auction was purchased by Sharaswati, the wife of Darikanath. The sale certificate was issued to her on 01.08.1945. Thereafter she sold 2.22 acres of land by a kabala dated 08.02.1946 in favour of Mohendra and Dhirendra. She again transferred 0.55 acres of land by a patta dated 21.02.1951 in favour of defendant No.7 and again transferred 1.05 acres of land by another patta dated 25.04.1953 in favour of said defendant No.7. After those transfers she had possession in 0.62 acres of land but that land was wrongly recorded in the name of Mohendra and Dhirendra. The said Sharaswati sold that 0.62 acres of land by a kabala dated 06.10.1983 in favour of Nirmalkanti. Thereafter she filed the Title Suit No. 511 of 1983 for correction of the SA record in respect of 0 .62 decimals impleading the plaintiffs to be defendant Nos. 1 and 2 and got an exparte decree on 27.04.1955. It is his further case that Mohendra and Dhirendra left for India in 1965 and their shares were declared as Enemy Property. The plaintiff No.1 had taken lease of 2.37 acres from the Enemy Property Authority vide the Miscellaneous Case No.11(Ka) of 7273. That lease was continued till 1990 and thereafter the defendant no. 1 took lease of said land from the Enemy Property Authority. It is the further case of the defendant no.1 that he purchased .77 decimals of land from the defendant No.7. 

 14. On the otherhand the defendant No. l's case is that the entire land of the jote was sold in auction in Title Execution Case No, 133 of 1944 and that was purchased by Saraswati. It is his further case that Saraswati was exhausted by the transfers made by kabala dated 08.02.1946, 06.10.1983 and by patta dated 21.02.1951 and 25.04.1953. Lastly his case is that the plaintiffs have neither title nor possession in the suit land. 

 16. But it appears from the record that the court of Appeal below as the last court of facts concurred with the findings of the Trial Court that the Saraswati acquired the title and possession in respect of entire 4.44 acres of land belonging to predecessors of the plaintiffs by way of auction purchase in Execution Case No. 133 of 1944 and that this defendant No. 1 submitted: the writ of delivery of possession vide exhibit "Uma" in support of title of said Sharaswati. The high court division was wrong in finding that no title passed in favour of transferees from Sharaswati by kabala deed dated 04.02.1946, by patta dated 21.02.1951, 25.04.1953 and the deed dated 06.10.1983 upon an erroneous view that the auction purchase by Sharaswati is not supported by any delivery of possession.
